snippet.title: When a drink feels like you’re cheating on your loved one | Oatly
snippet.description:
People have been calling this film of Pink Dragon Matcha from the Oatly and Nespresso collaboration food porn, and we’re outraged. Seriously, people—grow up! Pink Dragon Matcha isn’t food. It’s a drink.

Pink Dragon Mocha
All You Need

1 Oatly x Nespresso capsule ice
220 g ice
190 ml Oatly Barista Edition
20 ml white chocolate syrup
2 g dragon fruit powder

To-Do List
Add Oatly Barista Edition to Aeroccino and froth on cold setting.
Add frothed Oatly and dragon fruit powder to a jug and stir until combined.
Pull a shot of Nespresso x Oatly capsule over white chocolate syrup and stir to combine.
Add ice, followed by the dragon fruit and Oatly froth, then white chocolate espresso to a glass.

snippet.title: Pee for the Planet — Your Pee. The fertilizer of the future | Oatly
snippet.description:
What if the solution to one of agriculture’s biggest climate challenges is right in front of us? Or, more accurately, down the drain. MFF football players Otto Rosengren and Taha Ali tell you all about it in a film made at the heart of this project, Eleda Stadion.
 
We’re now launching Pee for the Planet – a research project funded by Formas, initiated by Oatly, Malmö FF, Sanitation 360 and SLU, in collaboration with City of Malmö and VA Syd.
 
From 24th of May and onward during Allsvenskan season, we’ll start collecting football supporters’ pee at MFF’s home ground arena. There will be a number of remodeled toilets and urinals at the site, and the goal is to transform it into a circular alternative to fossil based synthetic fertilizer, with the aim of using it for farming of both oat fields and football pitches.
 
Human urine contains the nutrients that crops need and can in theory replace up to 30% of the synthetic fertilizers used in Sweden today. This means it could be a possibility to decrease the dependency on imported and fossil based synthetic fertilizer, and therefore strengthen the food production for the future.
 
Read more about the project at peefortheplanet.com

snippet.title: Loba Pastry + Coffee | Café con el Abuelo | Oatly
snippet.description:
Luis is a coffee drinker. He loves telling baristas that. He also apparently loves pairing his smoked vanilla latte with a sweet treat. Whic means Jeremy knew exactly what he was doing when he took his abuelo to Loba Pastry + Cofee, ordered one of everything in the pastry case, and whispered, “Don’t worry. Oatly’s paying for it.”

About the Series:
Introducing the planet’s next great pair of coffee influencers: an overeager Oatly employee named Jeremy and his sweet 85-year-old abuelo, Luis. Together they set out on a tour of Chicago's best cafés to taste and review fancy coffees, iced matchas, ube lattes, espresso tonics, and whatever else the baristas wanted to pour that day.

Most of the drinks were made with Oatly, but all of them were made to impress Luis, who’s been drinking coffee since he was a four-year-old growing up in Puerto Rico. That’s what he told us at least. We didn’t attempt to verify his claim—nor do we plan to. It’s a better story this way.

snippet.title: Gnocchi panna e salmone | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #26: Might rebrand as Oatly couples therapy 


Gnocchi panna e salmone 

Ingredients: 

For the gnocchi: 
1 kg red potatoes 
300 g 00 flour  
1 medium egg 
Fine salt to taste 
Durum semolina flour to dust the dough 

 
For the sauce: 
200 g smoked salmon 
500 ml Oatly Creamy Oat 
Extra virgin olive oil 
Salt to taste 
Pepper to taste 

 
Peel the potatoes, boil until tender, and mash them. Mix the mashed potatoes with flour, egg, and salt to form a dough. Roll the dough into logs and cut into bite-sized pieces to form gnocchi. Dust with semolina.  


Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float to the surface, then drain. In a pan, heat some olive oil and add the smoked salmon, cooking gently.  
 

Add the Oatly Creamy Oat and stir until the sauce thickens slightly. Toss the cooked gnocchi in the salmon cream sauce, season with salt and pepper, top with plant-based parmesan and fresh Italian herbs, and serve hot.

snippet.title: Delizie al limone | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #07: Very satisfashion one 


Delizie al limone 

Ingredients: 
3 eggs 
35 g white sugar 
35 ml neutral oil 
25 g 00 flour  
1 1/2 lemons 
Lemon extract (a few drops) 
250 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat 
125 ml Oatly Oatgurt Greek Style 
Fresh mint (for decorating) 

 
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). In a bowl, whisk the eggs and white sugar until light and fluffy. Gradually add the neutral oil while continuing to whisk. Sift the flour and gently fold it into the egg mixture. Grate the zest of the lemons and squeeze the juice, adding both to the mixture along with the lemon extract. Pour the batter into greased molds and bake for about 20 to 25 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.  


While the cakes cool, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. Mix the whipped cream with Oatly Oatgurt Greek Style and a few drops of lemon extract. Once the sponge cakes are cool, dig a small hole in the center of the flat side (keep the cap aside for now) and fill them with the cream.  

 
Close with the cap of sponge cake. Cover the cakes with the leftover creamy mixture. On the top of each dome, form a tuft of cream with a piping bag and decorate with fresh mint.

snippet.title: Sformatini di asparagi | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #22: Queen Vittoria 

Sformatini di asparagi 
Ingredients: 
1 bunch of asparagus 
200 ml Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche 
3 eggs 
Plant-based parmesan 
Salt and pepper 
2 tbsp plant-based butter 
Breadcrumbs 
1 tbsp flour  

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Clean and trim the asparagus, then boil until tender. Puree together with the Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche.  


In a bowl, whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the asparagus puree, grated plant-based parmesan, and a pinch of salt to the egg mixture.  
 

Grease small molds with plant-based butter and coat with grated breadcrumbs. Pour the mixture into the molds and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until set and golden on top. Serve warm and garnish with more grated plant-based parmesan. 

 –––––– Find out more about Oatly here: https://www.oatly.com https://www.instagram.com/oatly https://www.tiktok.com/@oatly

snippet.title: Cacio e pepe | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #15: Yes, yes, we like, we like 

Cacio e pepe 
Ingredients: 

For the pasta: 
100 g 00 flour  
1 medium egg (approx. 55 g) 
 

For the sauce: 
4 tbsp Oatly Oat Drink 
20 g plant-based parmesan 
Black pepper 
Salt 
 

Prepare the pasta by mixing the flour and egg until a smooth dough forms. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes. In a pasta machine or by hand, roll out the pasta dough and cut into tagliatelle. Boil water with a generous pinch of salt, then add your pasta (note that fresh pasta takes roughly 2 to 3 minutes to cook).  
 

Grate the plant-based parmesan in a bowl and mix in the Oatly Oat Drink and a pinch of salt. Put a pan on medium heat and toast a generous amount of black pepper until it becomes fragrant. Add a small scoop of the pasta water. Mix and turn off the heat.  

 
Lift pasta out of the pasta water and add to the pan with pepper. Add the plant-based parmesan and oat drink mixture and stir together well. Put pasta on a plate, top with extra black pepper, and serve immediately. 

 –––––– Find out more about Oatly here: https://www.oatly.com https://www.instagram.com/oatly https://www.tiktok.com/@oatly

snippet.title: Maritozzi & coffee | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #10: The most important meal of the day 

Maritozzi buns 
Ingredients: 
500 g 0 flour  
90 g white sugar 
5 g instant dry yeast 
250 ml + 3 tbsp of Oatly Oat Drink Regular 
90 ml neutral oil (plus extra for brushing on dough) 
Zest of 1 orange 
Zest of 1 lemon 
1 tbsp maple syrup 
Pinch of salt 
2 tsp vanilla extract 
140 g white sugar (for syrup), plus extra for sprinkling on top 
400 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat 
Powdered sugar for dusting  

Dissolve the yeast in 250 ml of Oatly Oat Drink at room temperature. Mix the flour and 90 g white sugar in a bowl and add the oil and Oat Drink mixture. Add the orange and lemon zest, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt and mix well to a soft consistency.  

Knead the dough for about 10 minutes without adding any more flour. If necessary, wet your hands with a little oil. Then place the dough in a bowl, brush it with oil, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in the oven (turned off) until doubled in volume (3 to 4 hours). 
 
Divide the dough into eight equal pieces (80 g each), form into balls, and stretch them gently. Let them rise again for about an hour, well covered, and then brush them lightly with the 3 tbsp of Oatly Oat Drink and bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 15 minutes.  


To make the maritozzi shiny, prepare a syrup by dissolving 140 g of sugar with 100 ml of water in a saucepan. Once the maritozzi are baked and still hot, brush them with syrup and sprinkle with a bit of sugar. 

 
Whip the Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat while the buns are cooling down. Once the buns have cooled, split them down the center without dividing them in half, open them a little, and stuff with the whipped Oatly using a scoop. The whipped Oatly should be leveled well so that it does not come out excessively. Dust them with powdered sugar and enjoy with a cup of coffee.

snippet.title: Tiramisu | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #02: The Italian way is the only way 


Tiramisu 

Ingredients: 
5 egg yolks (pasteurized) 
150 g white sugar 
250 ml Oatly Vanilla Custard 
150 g Oatly Creamy Oat Spread 
300 g Savoiardi biscuits 
300 ml brewed coffee, cooled (preferably a strong coffee) 
250 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat 
2 tbsp cocoa powder (for dusting) 
 
Brew coffee using a moka pot or any other method. Allow it to cool completely.  

In a bowl, whisk together the pasteurized egg yolks and white sugar until the mixture is thick and pale. This should take about 5 to 7 minutes. Whisk in the Oatly Vanilla Custard, then gently fold the Oatly Creamy Oat Spread into the egg yolk mixture until smooth and well combined. Be careful not to deflate the mixture too much. 


To assemble tiramisu, quickly dip each biscuit into the cooled coffee, making sure not to soak them for too long to avoid sogginess. Arrange a layer of soaked biscuits at the bottom of a 22 x 16 cm dish. Spread half of the creamy mixture over the biscuits, smoothing the top with a spatula. Repeat with another layer of coffee-soaked biscuits and then spread the remaining mixture on top. 
 

Whip the Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat until stiff peaks form and use it to decorate the top of the tiramisu. Dust the top generously with cocoa powder. 

 
Cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the tiramisu to set. Before serving, dust with a bit more cocoa powder if desired. 

 –––––– Find out more about Oatly here: https://www.oatly.com https://www.instagram.com/oatly https://www.tiktok.com/@oatly

snippet.title: Cannelonely Cannelloni | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #37: Cannelonely … it’s a pun 

 

Cannelonely Cannelloni 
Ingredients: 
For the pasta (8 cannelloni): 
100 g 00 flour  
1 medium egg (approx. 55 g) 
 

For the filling: 
250 g spinach 
200 ml Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche 
1 medium egg 
Grated plant-based parmesan 
1 garlic clove, minced 
Pinch of nutmeg 
Extra virgin olive oil to taste 
Fine salt to taste 
Black pepper to taste 
 

For the béchamel sauce: 
50 g plant-based butter 
37 g 00 flour  
500 ml Oatly Oat Drink 
Nutmeg to taste 
Pinch of fine salt  
Pinch of black pepper 
 

Prepare the pasta by mixing the flour and eggs until a smooth dough forms. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets and cut into rectangles for cannelloni.  
 

Cook the spinach, drain well, and chop finely. In a bowl, mix the spinach, Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche, egg, grated plant-based parmesan, minced garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper to form the filling.  
 

For the béchamel, melt the plant-based butter in a saucepan, add the flour, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring often. Gradually add the Oatly Oat Drink, whisking constantly, until thickened. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.  

 
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Fill the pasta rectangles with the spinach mixture and roll them into cannelloni. Spread a layer of béchamel sauce in a baking dish, place the cannelloni on top, and cover with more béchamel sauce. Sprinkle grated plant-based parmesan over the top and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden and bubbly.

snippet.title: Riso e latte | Casting tape cooking | Oatly
snippet.description:
Audition #34: Behold the simplest recipe on earth 


Riso e latte 

Ingredients: 
300 g carnaroli rice (or arborio rice) 
1.5 L Oatly Oat Drink Whole 
2 tbsp olive oil 
Pinch of salt 
Pinch of pepper 
Plant-based parmesan to taste 
Fresh herbs to garnish 
 

In a large saucepan, bring the Oatly Oat Drink to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Add a pinch of salt. Gradually stir in the rice, ensuring it doesn’t lump together. Cook the rice in the oat drink, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until the rice is tender and has absorbed most of the oat drink. Stir in the olive oil. Once the rice is cooked, remove it from the heat and stir in grated plant-based parmesan to taste. Top with more plant-based parmesan and fresh herbs and serve hot as a creamy, comforting dish.

snippet.title: Audition #05: Whistle while you work—or maybe don’t | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Butternut Squash & Sage Risotto

Ingredients (serves 4):
1 big-ish butternut squash
1 tsp honey
A couple of decent glugs of olive oil
A couple of handfuls of fresh sage
1 spoonful dried rosemary
1 spoonsful dried thyme
1 large shallot
Plant-based butter
300 g Arborio rice
1 bottle of (nice) nonalcoholic white wine (chilled)
1/2 g saffron
Vegetable stock
Big dollop of Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche
Plant-Based Parmesan
150 g cashew nuts
1 pinch garlic powder
1 pinch mustard powder
4 tbsp nutritional yeast

Prep the squash, peeling it and cutting it into 3 cm chunks. Then coat with olive oil and honey, followed by chopped sage, rosemary, and thyme. Roast the squash in the oven at 200°C for about half an hour.

While that’s roasting, chop the shallot and fry it gently in the pan with the butter. After about 5 minutes, add risotto rice and keep stirring over the heat until the rice has turned glossy.

Pour in the wine and boil until it has reduced completely. Turn down the heat and gradually add the stock a little bit at a time until the rice is cooked and the stock has been absorbed.

While the risotto is cooking, chuck the cashews, garlic powder, mustard powder, yeast, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blitz to a fine powder—this will be the “parmesan.” Fry the sage leaves in oil until nice and crispy.

By now, the squash should be about ready. Take it out of the oven and mash most of it up, saving a few chunks. Stir the mashed squash into the risotto along with a spoonful of the Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche and a little bit of butter.

Plate the risotto and scatter the remaining chunks of roasted squash and crispy sage, plus a good sprinkling of the homemade parmesan.

snippet.title: Audition #14: Pearls of wisdom with a side of mash | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Fish, Peas & Mash

Ingredients (serves 2):
1 bag of organic potatoes (Maris Piper or King Edward)
2 garlic cloves
1 pack of organic parsley
1 L Oatly Oat Drink Whole
2 sustainably sourced cod loins (150 g each)
1 pack of organic petit pois (green peas)
1 tbsp plain flour
3 tbsp water
250 ml Oatly Creamy Oat
White pepper
Black pepper
Salt
Lemon wedge

Peel, chop, and put potatoes on a boil. Chop 2 cloves of garlic and parsley quite fine. Pour Oatly Oat Drink into a wide-bottomed pan and season with salt and chopped garlic. Put over a low heat and warm the oat drink to a gentle simmer. Place the cod in the oat drink and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, depending on the thickness of the fish.

Meanwhile, boil the green peas in a small pot. Once the cod has poached, remove from the pan. Cover with foil or place in an oven set to low so that it keeps warm. Make a slurry using plain flour and water. Add this to the pan of poaching liquid. Stir on medium heat until the sauce thickens. Season generously with black pepper and chopped parsley. Make the mash by first draining the boiled potatoes. Then add Oatly Creamy Oat and mash together. Season with salt and pepper.

To serve, place a generous portion of mash on a plate alongside the peas. Place poached cod and cover in the garlicky oaty sauce. Garnish with a wedge of lemon.

Loso na Madesu

Ingredients (serves 4):
1 large leek (finely sliced)
2 cans of butter beans (drained)
2 cans of chopped tomatoes
4 tbsp sunflower oil
1/2 tsp turmeric
1/2 tsp nutmeg
1/2 tsp paprika
1 tsp curry powder
1 tsp mixed herbs
2 bay leaf
Salt & pepper
*Secret Seasoning*
200 g basmati rice
125 ml Oatly Creamy Oat
200 ml hot water
Coconut and spring onions to garnish

Place a wide-based saucepan on medium heat. Add sunflower oil and the finely sliced leeks. Sautee for 5 minutes until softened. Then add all of your spices and cook for a further 2 minutes, before adding in your canned tomatoes and beans. This should cook gently for 20 to 30 minutes.

Midway through that, put your rice on to cook. Rinse rice under cold water, then add it to a rice cooker with the hot water and Oatly Creamy Oat. If cooking rice on the hob, place in a medium saucepan, bring to a simmer for 5 minutes, then reduce heat to low. Place on the lid and steam for 8 minutes.

To finish your beans, first add that special secret seasoning. Then serve a generous portion in a bowl and top with coconut and spring onion.

snippet.title: Audition #30: Cheers, darlings | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Eton Mess

Ingredients (serves 2-4):
2 large egg whites (or 6 tbsp of aquafaba)
120 g caster sugar
500 g strawberries, hulled and roughly chopped
450 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat
1 tbsp icing sugar
Non-alcoholic sparkling wine

Heat oven to 120°C/100°C fan/gas and line a large baking tray with parchment paper.

Whisk the egg whites (or aquafaba) in a super duper clean bowl using an electric whisk—or try hand-held if you want to give yourself a cheeky arm workout. Whisk until they reach stiff peaks. Then add the sugar in thirds whilst you keep whisking.

Spoon dollops of the mixture onto the baking parchment. Cook on the bottom shelf of the oven for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the meringues are completely hard and easily slide off the paper.

When meringues are in the oven, soak the strawberries in a gorgeous bowl of champagne— preferably Veuve or Dom—and, most importantly, pour yourself a glass. Then make sure there is enough to pour yourself many more glasses. (The strawberries should soak for 1 to
4 hours, so may need to soak them in advance of the meringues.)

Whizz up 1/3 of the strawberries to make a strawberry sauce. Chop most of the remaining strawberries. Leave a strawberry per serving, and coat it in caster sugar to add a bit of panache.

In a large bowl, whisk the cream with the icing sugar until it just holds its shape. Soft peaks only, please!

Roughly crush 3/4 of the meringues and tip them in with the chopped strawberries and stir. Then swirl through the strawberry sauce. Dollop into bowls and crush the remaining meringues, sprinkling the pieces over the top. Place the sugar-coated, champagne-soaked strawberry on top and … tadaaaah!

Enjoy with more champagne and hopefully you’ll feel as messy as an Eton Boy!

snippet.title: Audition #18: Make hotgirl progress in your life | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Hotgirl Avo Toast
Ingredients (serves 1-2):

Puree
2 ripe avocados
Oatly Creamy Oat Spread
1 lemon
Salt & pepper

Toppings
2 large slices of sourdough bread
1 tbsp plant-based butter
2 large eggs
1 bunch of chives
6 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 block plant-based halloumi
2 tbsp honey
2 tbsp chlli flakes
Mixed seeds (e.g. pumpkin, sunflower seeds)
Watercress

To make the puree, cut and remove skin from avocados. Put avocados in a blender with a heaping spoonful of Oatly Creamy Oat Spread. Add salt and pepper and squeeze the juice of half a lemon. Blend until puree is formed. Scoop puree into an icing bag.

Next, spread plant-based butter on slices of sourdough bread. Toast both sides of bread in a
heated pan.

To poach eggs, crack egg and remove excess liquid by sieving egg into a bowl. Bring water to pre boil in a saucepan and reduce heat. Add salt to water. Whisk lightly until the water is spinning and slowly drop in the egg. Allow to cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Drain on paper towel and add cracked pepper on top.

For the chive oil, chop the bunch of chives in half and add to blender. Add extra virgin olive oil and blend until all bits disappear. Through a milk strainer, drain into a bowl. Add into a squeeze bottle.

Then chop plant-based halloumi into slices. Add honey and chili flakes to the halloumi and then fry in a saucepan. Heat on low for 2 minutes.

To plate, put toast on board. Using the piping bag, pipe the avocado puree onto the toast in a zigzag motion. Drizzle the chive oil using a spoon. Add halloumi and poached eggs on top. Sprinkle on mixed seeds and finish with watercress.

snippet.description:
Creamy Mushroom Tagliatelle

Ingredients (serves 2-3):
2 shallots
2 garlic cloves
4 portobello mushrooms
1 tbsp garlic-infused oil
A bit of plant-based butter
100 ml nonalcoholic white wine
250 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat
75 g Oatly Creamy Oat Spread
400 g fresh tagliatelle
1 egg yolk
A handful of plant-based parmesan
Fresh parsley
Fresh chives
Rocket/arugula
Salt & pepper

Finely dice the shallots and garlic cloves and slice the mushrooms. Heat the garlic-infused oil in a wide-based saucepan. Add the shallots and garlic and let them sweat for 5 minutes.

Next, add the sliced mushrooms, plant-based butter, and parsley. Cook for 5 more minutes. Add the nonalcoholic white wine, lots of seasoning (salt and pepper), Oatly Creamy Oat, and Oatly Creamy Oat Spread. Let simmer for 5 minutes.

Set a medium saucepan of salted boiling water on the hob. Cook fresh tagliatelle to packet instructions. Drain the pasta and add it to the pan of mushroom sauce. Remove pan from the heat before stirring in egg yolk and a handful of grated parmesan.

Plate the pasta and garnish with more parmesan, chives, garlic oil, and rocket.

snippet.title: Audition #23: It was all yellow … Sophie, not the galette | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Heirloom Tomato Galette
Ingredients (serves 4):

Filling
600 g heirloom tomatoes of various colours and sizes
1/2 tsp fennel seeds
Oatly Creamy Oat Spread
2 cloves of garlic
1 bunch of fresh basil
Extra virgin olive oil
Salt & pepper

Pastry
250 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
150 g cold, salted plant-based butter, cut into cubes
2 eggs
2 tbsp poppy seeds or nigella seeds
4-5 tbsp water

Cut tomatoes into 1 cm slices and sprinkle a tsp of salt over them. Leave in a colander to draw out some of the moisture. 

Meanwhile, make the pastry. Add flour and salt to a food processor, and slowly add in the cubed butter. When it reaches a crumb-like texture, crack in one egg. Then add the poppy seeds. Gradually pour in ice cold water a tbsp at a time until the mix forms a round dough ball. Flatten the ball, cover it in cling film, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 225°C. Grate the garlic into the Oatly Creamy Oat Spread and season with salt and pepper. Drain tomatoes and toss in olive oil with the fennel seeds. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the pastry to a large disk around 1.5 cm thick. Transfer to
a lined baking dish. Spread the creamy oat over the middle of the pastry making sure to leave a 2-inch border. Place the tomatoes evenly on top. Fold over the edge to create a crust and brush with beaten egg and season with salt.

Bake 30 to 40 minutes until golden brown. Scatter some freshly picked basil leaves on top and drizz with olive oil.

snippet.title: Audition #32: Too many cooks in the kitchen is a good thing | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Vegetable Lasagna
Ingredients (serves 4):

Filling
2 red peppers
2 aubergines
150 g cherry tomatoes
300 g lasagne sheets
125 g grated plant-based cheese

Tomato Sauce
Olive oil
2 onions
2 garlic cloves
1 carrot
2 tbsp tomato puree
200 ml nonalcoholic white wine
2 x 400 g chopped tomatoes
1 bunch of fresh basil
1/2 tub of Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche

White sauce
50 g plain flour
50 g plant-based butter
500 ml Oatly Oat Drink Whole
1 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp nutmeg
Salt & pepper

Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C Fan/Gas 6.

Cut up the aubergine, peppers, and cherry tomatoes and mix them in a bowl with olive oil and seasoning. Put in the oven to roast (best on a tray) until lightly browned (approximately 20 to 25 min).

To make the tomato sauce, heat olive oil in a large, nonstick saucepan and fry the diced onion, stirring regularly, for 3 to 4 minutes—or until softened and lightly browned. Chop the carrots and fry, stirring regularly. Add the diced garlic, tomato puree, nonalcoholic white wine, chopped tomatoes, and Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche (save the basil until the end). Cook until tasty (10 to 15 minutes), adding water if needed.

To make the white sauce, heat plant-based butter in a medium saucepan. When it’s hot, add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Stir in the Oatly Oat Drink Whole, garlic powder, and nutmeg, and season well with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly with a metal whisk over a moderate heat for 4 to 5 minutes—or until smooth and
thickened. Adjust the seasoning to taste.

Layer the lasagna, mixing the oven-baked aubergine and peppers with the white sauce and red sauce. Garnish with plant-based cheese in between or just on the top. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, or until the pasta has softened and the topping is nicely browned and bubbling. Stand for 5 minutes before cutting to allow the filling to settle.

snippet.title: Audition 12: The poetry slam scene has been real quiet since this dropped | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Panna cotta

Ingredients (serves 6):
5 dl Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat (or 2.5 dl Whippable + 2.5 dl Vanilla Custard)
1 dl sugar
1 tsp agar agar or 2.5 sheets of gelatine
2 tsp vanilla sugar

Pour the liquids into a small pot, add the caster sugar, and bring to a boil. Add the vanilla sugar.

If you’re using agar agar: add it to the pot, stir, and let simmer until it starts to thicken.

If you’re using gelatine: soak the gelatine sheets in water for 5mins before transferring them to the pot. Stir and let simmer until it thickens.

Remove from the heat once the liquid has thickened. Pour the liquid into 6 small glasses and leave to set in the fridge for an hour or two.

Once set, decorate and garnish as you please (Annelie used: wafer rolls, sea buckthorn, persimmon, orange jam, and edible gold dust), and enjoy.

snippet.title: Audition 44: The stress of cooking with mom | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Kousa Bil Laban (Stuffed Zucchini with Oatgurt Sauce)

Ingredients (serves 4 to 5):
2 cups rice
1 cup vermicelli
300g plant-based mince
1000g small zucchinis
500ml Oatly Oatgurt Turkish
1 cup Oatly Oat Drink Whole
0,5 tsp Cinnamon
Pinch of White pepper
Pinch of Black pepper
Salt
1 tsp Lebanese pepper (allspice)
1 tsp Za’atar
1 tsp Garlic powder
2 tbsp Cornstarch
1 tsp Dried mint
Olive oil
Fresh mint (optional)

Rinse the rice and leave it to soak in water for 20 minutes. Heat oil in a medium pot and add vermicelli, stirring it until toasted and golden brown. Add the rice and stir until everything is coated with the oil.

Add 3 1/2 cups of water and bring to boil. Once water starts reducing, turn heat to low, cover with lid, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes. When done, let rest for another 10 minutes with the lid on.

Fry the plant-based mince in oil in a pan until it browns. Add cinnamon, white pepper, black pepper, salt, za’atar, and Lebanese pepper and fry for another 2 minutes. Set aside.

Cut off the tops of the zucchinis and carefully hollow them out with a peeler or teaspoon. Don’t carve them too thin. Heat oil in a pan and fry the hollowed zucchinis 3 to 4 minutes to brown them all around.

Leave them to cool and dry on a paper towel. Once cooled, fill them with the vegetarian mince.

Place a strainer over a large pot and pour in the Oatgurt along with garlic powder, cornstarch, and dried mint. Pour in the oat drink and stir together through the strainer and into the pot. Turn on the heat and bring to a boil. Once at a boil, immediately lower to a simmer and continue to stir as it simmers. Gently add the filled zucchinis, make sure they are covered by the sauce, and let simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.

Serve with rice and top with some optional fresh mint.

snippet.title: Audition 21: Ehsan spilling the tea | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Scones & Tea

Ingredients (makes 10 scones):

Scones
400 ml rolled oats
2 tsp baking soda
Pinch of salt
Pinch of brown sugar
50 g plant-based butter
200 ml Oatly Oatgurt Turkish
1/2 g saffron
Jam of your choice

Tea
Fresh ginger
Cinnamon stick
Cardamom pod (crushed)
Hot water
Black tea
Star anise
1 tbsp Honey
A dash of Oatly Oat Drink

Heat the oven to 225°C (440°F). In a bowl, mix the rolled oats with baking soda, salt, and sugar. Mix in the plant-based butter. Add the Oatgurt and saffron and quickly mix into a sticky dough.

Distribute the dough into 10 circles onto baking paper on a baking tray (spatulas are helpful tools for this). Pop them into the oven for 8 to 12 minutes, or until golden. Set aside to cool.

To make the tea: bring water to a boil and add fresh ginger, cinnamon, and the crushed cardamom pod. Leave to simmer for 10 minutes. Turn the stove off. Add a few teaspoons of black tea and let sit for another 3 to 4 minutes. Add a dash of oat drink and honey and let sit for another 5 minutes. Pour the tea through a tea strainer and into a teapot.

Once the tea is done and the scones are cool enough to eat, serve the scones with a tasty jam and the tea in small cups with a piece of star anise.

snippet.description:
Marängsviss (aka Swedish ice-cream mountain)

Ingredients:
Oatly ice-cream flavours of your choice
250 ml Oatly Creamy Oat
100 g plant-based chocolate
Pinch of salt
250 ml Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat
Plant-based meringues (or whatever kinds of meringues you like)
Fresh fruits and berries to garnish
Sprinkles, sweets, and/or peanuts to garnish (optional)

Start by melting the chocolate in a water bath. Add the Oatly Creamy Oat and stir until completely combined. Turn the heat off and set aside.

Whisk the Oatly Whippable Creamy Oat until fluffy (add vanilla powder here if you’d like, but this is optional).

Assemble by laying scoops of ice cream in a big serving bowl and top with the creamy oat. Drizzle over chocolate sauce, meringues, fresh fruits and berries, and potential toppings of your liking. Enjoy!

snippet.title: Audition 3: Welsh Cakes by Nathan (in one take) | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Welsh Cakes 

Ingredients:

For the cakes:
225g flour + extra for dusting
1 tsp baking powder
1/4 tsp fine sea salt
1 tsp nutmeg, grated
1/2 tsp British mixed spice
100g dairy-free butter
50g caster sugar + extra to sprinkle
50g sultanas
1 cup of freshly brewed English breakfast tea
3–4 tbsp Oatly Oat Drink
1 tbsp Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche
Extra dairy-free butter for frying the cakes
100g granulated sugar
1 tsp of blueberry powder (optional)

For the fraiche:
1 pot Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche
50g frozen bilberries or blueberries
2–3 freshly ground cardamom pods
Zest and juice of half a lemon
1 tbsp bilberry or blueberry jam
Crushed black pepper

Welsh Cakes method:
1. Pre-soak the sultanas in warm tea and leave until plump, then drain.
2. Combine the dry ingredients in a large bowl. Add the butter and mix until it reaches a fine, breadcrumb consistency
3. Add the sugar and pre-soaked sultanas and stir in the Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche. Then add the 3 tbsp of Oat Drink until the mixture comes together (add another 1 tbsp if the dough is a little dry)
4. Bring together into a ball, try not to overwork the dough as this will make it tough
5. Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to a 5mm thickness and cut out rounds using a 7 or 8 cm cutter. Re-roll any scraps and cut out more until you have used up all the dough
6. Place a heavy based frying pan over a medium heat
7. Grease the pan with a nob of plant-based butter (re-grease before each new batch of cakes in the pan). Cook the cakes for 3–4 mins on each side, or until lightly golden. Once fried, immediately toss the cakes in the sugar and set aside on a wire rack to cool down

Fraiche method:
1. Mix the bilberries/blueberries in the sugar and lemon juice, set aside for 10-15 minutes
2. Grind the cardamom pods in a pestle and mortar
3. Spoon some of the bilberries/blueberries and lemon juice
into a small mixing bowl. Add the ground cardamom, jam, lemon zest, and black pepper (add a bit more juice from the macerating juice if needed).
4. Fold the Oatly Creamy Oat Fraiche into the mixture with a spatula, leaving it slightly marbled
5. Plate the cakes with some marbled fraiche topped with extra bilberries/blueberries

snippet.title: Audition 57: She’s not like a regular chef, she’s a cool chef | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Shahi Paneer

Ingredients (serves 4–5 people):
300g paneer
3 tbsp oil
2 tsp butter
1 tsp cumin seeds
1 pinch of asafoetida
4 cloves
1 cinnamon stick
A pinch of nutmeg
1/4 tsp turmeric
1/4 tsp of red chili powder
1/2 cup onion
1/2 tsp cardamom
1/2 tsp of paprika powder
1 tsp salt
1 tsp sugar
1 tsp garam masala
2 tbsp chopped cilantro/coriander
1 tbsp ginger
1 tbsp garlic
3 green chilies
1 tbsp kasturi methi
2 tomatoes
1 tsp tomato purée
1/2 cup of Oatly Oatgurt Turkish
1⁄4 cup Oatly Creamy Oat

Method:
1. Heat a pan with oil and add sliced onions, tomatoes, green chilies, sliced garlic, and sliced ginger. Sauté for around 8 mins, then cool it down and blend in a mixer to a fine paste
2. In the same pan, add a little bit of butter and oil along with the crushed cumin seeds, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Add the garam masala, turmeric, red chili powder. Add the blended tomato onion paste kept aside, along with kasturi methi, and 1/2 cup of Oatly Oatgurt. Lastly, add the salt and sugar
3. In another pan, add a bit of oil and fry the chopped paneer with a pinch of nutmeg
4. Once fried and golden, add the paneer to the other pan. Mix in the Oatly Creamy Oat. Top it off with fresh cilantro/coriander and enjoy

2 tbsp chopped cilantro/coriander
1 tbsp ginger
1 tbsp garlic
3 green chilies
1 tbsp kasturi methi
2 tomatoes
1 tsp tomato purée
1/2 cup of Oatly Oatgurt Turkish
1⁄4 cup Oatly Creamy Oat

Method:
1. Heat a pan with oil and add sliced onions, tomatoes, green chilies, sliced garlic, and sliced ginger. Sauté for around 8 mins, then cool it down and blend in a mixer to a fine paste
2. In the same pan, add a little bit of butter and oil along with the crushed cumin seeds, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Add the garam masala, turmeric, red chili powder. Add the blended tomato onion paste kept aside, along with kasturi methi, and 1/2 cup of Oatly Oatgurt. Lastly, add the salt and sugar
3. In another pan, add a bit of oil and fry the chopped paneer with a pinch of nutmeg
4. Once fried and golden, add the paneer to the other pan. Mix in the Oatly Creamy Oat. Top it off with fresh cilantro/coriander and enjoy

snippet.title: Audition 48: When in doubt, call your mom | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Steamed Pak Choi & Jamaican Festival

Ingredients (serves 4):
5 cloves of garlic
Half a red onion
5 lbs pak choi
8–10 cherry tomatoes
1/4 lb salted pollock
2 tbsp olive oil
250 ml Oatly Creamy Oat
1 sweet potato
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup fine cornmeal
6 tbsp granulated sugar
2 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
3/4 cup Oatly Oat Drink Whole
Natural oil for deep frying

Prepare your vegetables by smashing the garlic, cutting the red onion into big chunks, and chopping the pak choi. Slice the cherry tomatoes. Cut the pollock into bite-sized pieces.

In a wide saucepan over a medium-low heat, add the olive oil and garlic and stir for one minute. Add the red onion and cherry tomatoes and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Next, add the Oatly Creamy Oat and salted pieces of pollock. Stir and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes. Fold in the chopped pak choi (it might seem like a lot, but after a few minutes it will wilt and easily fit in the saucepan). Add a few pinches of salt (not too much since the fish is salted). Let cook at medium-low heat for about 25 minutes.

While that’s cooking, peel and chop the sweet potato. In a small pot, bring water to a boil and add sweet potatoes. Boil until soft.

To make the festival: In a large bowl, combine the flour, cornmeal, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir to combine and add the Oat Drink. Stir until the dough comes together. Then use your hands to lightly form the mixture into a ball. Pinch off pieces of dough and roll them into long oval shapes. The dough should make about 12 oval-shaped dumplings.

Heat a heavy bottom pot with at least 3 inches of frying oil (or use a deep fryer if you have one). Bring the heat to 350 degrees Fahrenheit (177 degrees Celsius). Once the oil has reached the correct temperature, add the dough dumplings. Fry them on all sides until golden brown. This takes about 4 to 6 minutes.

Take out the deep-fried dough dumplings with a slotted metal spoon and leave to drain off excess grease. Serve together with the pak choi and sweet potato and enjoy.

snippet.title: Audition 16: Yes, chef | #Shorts | Oatly
snippet.description:
Spinach & Basil Omelette
 
Ingredients (1 omelette):
4 eggs
50 g spinach
5 g basil
A knob of plant-based butter
A dash of olive oil
Oatly Creamy Oat Spread
1/2 shallot
2–3 leaves of kale
Zest of half a lemon
Salt & pepper

Bring water to boil in a medium pot. Add spinach and basil to blanch quickly. Fill a medium bowl with cold water and ice and put a strainer in it. Move the spinach and basil from the boiling water to an ice-bath bowl. Leave to cool.

Once cool, grab spinach and basil and squeeze firmly to remove all excess water. Put the ball of spinach and basil in a blender together with the 4 eggs. Mix until smooth and strain into a clean and empty bowl.

Prepare your kale by removing the stem and cut the leaves into smaller pieces. Heat a small pan with olive oil and cook the kale with salt for a few minutes. Set aside. (Optional: burn the kale with a flame torch to give it some extra flavour and colour.) Finely chop your shallot and set aside. 

Heat the small pan with plant-based butter. Add the spinach/basil/egg mixture, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and cook the omelette slowly. Once the omelette starts to set, add a dash of Oatly Creamy Oat Spread in the middle and fold the omelette with a spatula. Serve on a plate with the kale, and top it off with lemon zest and shallots.

snippet.title: The Giant Oatly Carton | Oatly
snippet.description:
After kindly being told to remove our Giant Oatly Carton from a professional baseball stadium in Texas, we wondered, “Who would actually want a 500-kilogram marketing prop with no conceivable real-world benefit?” The answer felt obvious: High school theater kids. But even with that part of the problem solved, we still had to figure out how to get the carton to them. Follow the Giant Oatly Carton on its journey from stadium to stage, where it’s been given new life in a popular musical we can’t name because we don’t have the rights and could potentially be sued.

snippet.title: Making Oatly Grasshoppers in America’s Dairy State | Will It Swap? | Oatly
snippet.description:
We thought it would be provocative to bring Oatly to Wisconsin—America’s Dairy State—and ask famed supper club The Duck Inn to use our products in its most popular dishes. The pitch to the Oatly execs was, “Dairy people trying non-dairy products. Chaos ensues.” Well, we went … but turns out there was no chaos. Just really kind people telling us how great our products are and asking us which channel our television show would air on. So with that underwhelming description, please enjoy our latest episode of “Will It Swap?,” in which we make Oatly grasshoppers, crème brûlées, clam chowders, pastas, and salmon in the heart of America’s dairy capital. Again, no chaos ensues.

snippet.title: The Oatly Dragster | Now as Fast as Dairy | Oatly
snippet.description:
Here at Oatly, we’re suckers for bizarre milk ephemera—mostly because it calls attention to how dated the concept of drinking milk actually is. We also have a soft spot for random exploits trying to prove that Oatly performs just as well as (if not better than) dairy. 

So, imagine our delight when we discovered that there’s a 1963 dairy truck puttering around the suburbs of Chicago. And that this dairy truck has been gutted and restored, peculiarly, as a real-life dragster by a very nice guy named Nick (with help from his dad and uncle).

In the end, we just couldn’t help ourselves. We visited Nick at his home in Manhattan, Illinois, with a simple idea: Let’s turn the dairy dragster plant-based and see how fast it goes.

Introducing the Oatly Dragster!

snippet.title: Design By Bulent | A London Deli Covered in Oatly
snippet.description:
Bulent Aslan may not be a name you hear listed among the world’s top interior designers, but in the very, very niche world of “Top Interior Designers Who Use Oatly Cartons As Wallpaper”, he is frequently cited as a global visionary. So of course we shamelessly invited ourselves into his London deli, Camia, and brought a camera operator, a producer, a director, a production assistant, and dozens of release forms. We had to meet the legend for an intimate and intrusive look at his art. 

Bulent is the genius behind groundbreaking work such as “Oatly carton as bathroom wallpaper” and “Oatly carton as hallway wallpaper” and “Oatly carton as kitchen wallpaper.” To see it all firsthand was an inspiration. When asked what feeds his ongoing creativity and passion, Bulent gave us the profound but indirect answer we were searching for: “I’m happy”.

snippet.title: U.S.S. Boatly | Yes, a boat made of Oatly
snippet.description:
This is a story about a boat, but it’s also a story about goodbyes. In the summer of 2022, a Colorado man named Nate had a vision: A boat made out of Oatly cartons. Most people wouldn’t act on such an insane vision, but Nate and his two children are not “most people”. And so, one of the greatest engineering feats of the last half century began.

Once complete, Nate and his brave (and also somewhat skeptical) children raced this beautifully branded canoe-like object down the Uncompahgre River in the 2022 Ridgway RiverFest. They won.  

That was in June. By the time we visited them in October, the great U.S.S. Boatly—it’s a brilliant play on words—was rotting outside Nate’s Colorado coffee shop. The sweet, pungent smell of fermenting river water and oat drink is an acquired taste—one apparently not acquired by the townspeople of Ridgway. And so, it was time to say goodbye to the engineering marvel that once proudly floated down a marvelous river very few people have ever heard of. 

Join us in saying goodbye to the U.S.S. Boatly.

snippet.description:
There are so many important questions you can ask yourself in life, and instead we asked this one: If you already love a place with a name that sounds sort of like a drink, will you also love that drink? snippet.title: Why does Oatly’s packaging look so weird?
snippet.description: Back in the day, we didn’t have much money for advertising, so we came up with a couple ideas to spread the word about our products. The first was to force everyone in the company to wear Oatly-branded shirts 24/7 and walk around the streets of Sweden as human billboards. Once we sketched it out on paper, this seemed like a bad idea. But the second idea ended up working out: Use all four sides of our packaging as a way to stand out on supermarket shelves and explain to people what we’re all about (without using robotic marketing language). You can find more nonrobotic marketing language on https://www.oatly.com

snippet.title: What’s with Oatly and the dairy lobby?
snippet.description: “What’s the deal with the dairy lobby?” sounds like a bad stand-up routine from the 1990s, but in 2014 it became a question we started asking ourselves frequently—probably because that’s the year the dairy lobby sued us. We were making a dairy alternative that was far less taxing on the planet and on many people’s bodies, and the lacto-sphere (that’s what the dairy lobby calls itself) had some serious issues with that, especially when we boasted about it while advertising our products. But who wants to get into a detailed legal discussion in the description section of a YouTube video? Exactly. So for nonlegal-related topics regarding Oatly, check out https://www.oatly.com

snippet.title: But why oats?
snippet.description: Why oats? Well, before we experimented with any products, we all fell in love with the name “Oatly,” and from then on, our options were pretty limited. But lucky for us, oats happen to be one of the most impressive grains on earth. They’re a highly efficient crop, they can be grown almost anywhere, they have a tremendous nutritional profile…and we’re all quite fond of the taste. There’s a more detailed list of attributes that includes terms such as beta-glucan, but this doesn’t exactly feel like the forum for that. For those sorts of details, head over to https://www.oatly.com

snippet.title: What do people get wrong about Oatly?
snippet.description: We know you didn’t come here to see a multinational oat company get all emo about consumer misperceptions, but it just feels like people don’t understand us a lot of the time. Maybe that’s a consequence of prioritizing quippy, self-referential advertising over clear product messaging. Whatever, we regret nothing. But, for the record, we’re not an oatmeal company, and we’re not some brand-new start-up from Silicon Valley. We’re just a bunch of weird Swedish oat nerds who have been obsessing over a single grain for the past three decades and make something pretty great with it. For more somewhat-accurate descriptions of who we are, head over to https://www.oatly.com

snippet.title: Where did Oatly come from?
snippet.description: This is where we take viewers on an immersive, 30-second journey to Sweden’s Lund University circa 1992, when our founder, Rickard Öste, first invented a gloriously delicious beverage made from oats. Because we weren’t able to secure the rights to any of the Swedish heavy metal music that dominated the cultural zeitgeist back then, the video is not as “immersive” as we initially intended—but, thankfully, we were able to secure Rickard Öste. For a fuller answer to your very important question, head over to https://www.oatly.com

snippet.title: Just Idag Är Jag Stark feat. Dragomir Mrsic | Varannan Havre | Oatly
snippet.description:
Det är inte alltid så enkelt att ändra livsstil. Att till exempel gå från att vara fullblodig köttätare till att bli renodlad vegan. Men om du gör det lite då och då? Typ varannan dag eller varannan frukost eller varannan fika. Då blir det förhoppningsvis lite lättare. Och oavsett hur velig du är, kommer du att få se resultat. Ta bara grädden. Om hälften av all kogrädde i Sverige ersattes av Oatly iMat skulle utsläppen av växthusgaser minska med mer än 230 000 ton CO2e.* Vilket motsvarar drygt 410 000 flygresor mellan Malmö och Madrid tur och retur.** (Varför man nu ska dra till Spanien när man kan promenera i Gröndal?) Nåja. Poängen är att många bäckar små och så vidare och så vidare.
 
*Underlag från Jordbruksverkets statistikdatabas, Konsumtion av livsmedel. Klimatavtryck produkter CarbonCloud AB, Sverige (2020). **Klimatsmartsemester.se.

snippet.title: Packaging | Stop AM 171 | Oatly
snippet.description: Soon — whatever that means in the political sphere — the EU will decide on amendment 171. And in case you haven’t heard, 171 is a proposed law for plant-based censorship, that could prohibit all use of dairy-related language, packaging and imagery for plant-based foods. It might even make it illegal to share scientific facts showing that a plant-based product has a lower climate footprint than its dairy alternative. Why? Well, the milk lobby seems to think that when plant-based products use descriptions like ”alternative to yogurt” or ”not milk” or ”creamy texture”, it’s hard for consumers to tell the difference between them and dairy. Eh, is it? We decided to find out if the people of Europe really are that stupid. Enjoy the film. And sign the petition at https://www.oatly.com/stopam171.

snippet.title: From Feed To Food | Oatly
snippet.description:
When making a documentary you should go all in, right? Black and white. Slow. Strange but visually cool camera angles. Touching piano music. A farmer talking about important things, like how to make farming both more sustainable and profitable, in a language that only a tiny part of the world’s population understands so you can use subtitles, since making people read during a movie lets them know they are learning. Nice touch. Yeah, our short documentary “From feed to food” definitely ends up with high scores on the test: ”How documentary is your documentary?” Although the end might contain a little too much success and hope for a documentary, but that’s just something you’ll have to live with.

Read more about the research done by UNISECO, a European research project: https://uniseco-project.eu/case-study/sweden

snippet.title: Nacho Boat | Oatly Department of Distraction Services
snippet.description:
Okay, so here’s the issue…If the point of this film from the Oatly Department of Distraction Services is to distract you from all the stuff we’re all trying to distract ourselves from these days…Then why (during this time of maximum distraction seeking) does this film reveal how two normally un-combinable distracting activities like nacho eating and bath time, can indeed be combined via a nacho boat, when these same two distracting activities, if performed separately, would result in greater distraction time in total? snippet.title: Wow No Cow | Toni TV | Oatly
snippet.description:
In a one of a kind performance, multi-talented CEO Toni Petersson sings a song he wrote entirely by himself to explain exactly what Oatly is all about. Please feel free to like, share and comment. Toni is a big boy, he can take it.

Music and lyrics written by Toni Petersson. Please feel free to use this song however you wish or make your own version and post it on youtube. Toni won’t care (as long as it is not better than the original).

Producer’s note: Toni TV was recorded in and around the organic oat fields of southern Sweden where Oatly has its offices. In order to ensure that viewers get to meet the real Toni Petersson, much of the footage was filmed without Toni’s knowledge that we were actually filming. Also, we didn’t let Toni view any of the material until just before it was released. Did we do this to trick Toni? Not entirely. We just felt that it was important for the viewer to get an honest idea of who the real Toni is and how Oatly — behind his new, offbeat, dynamic and visionary leadership — is becoming a lifestyle brand that makes nutritional products to help people find ways to upgrade their lives and the health of the planet too.
